title: Source Follower
intro: The source follower (common-drain stage) buffers a signal: it presents a high impedance to the source and a low impedance to the load.

blocks.text: The input drives the gate and the output is taken at the source, with a load RL or a current source. The output follows the input, a threshold-ish voltage lower.

blocks.source:
Av = gm*RL / [ 1 + (gm + gmb)*RL ]   (ro neglected)
Rout = 1 / (gm + gmb)
Vout = Vin - VTH - Vov   (a DC level shift)

items: Gain is below one and approaches gm/(gm+gmb) = 1/(1+eta) for large RL, so body effect caps the gain at around 0.8 to 0.9.
Output impedance 1/(gm+gmb) is low, which makes the follower a good buffer between a high-impedance node and a heavy load.
The level shift costs headroom: the output sits VGS below the input, and VGS rises with body effect.
Linearity is moderate: VTH changes with output voltage through the body effect, so use an NMOS in its own well when possible.

blocks.title: Gain with body effect
blocks.text: gm = 2 mS, gmb = 0.4 mS, RL = 2 kohm. Find Av and Rout.

blocks.title: Why the gain stays below one
blocks.text: Explain in one sentence why a source follower can never have a gain above one.
solution: The gate-source voltage that drives the current is Vin - Vout, and Vout = gm*RL*(Vin - Vout) at the source: solving gives Vout/Vin = gm*RL/(1 + gm*RL) < 1. Any rise in Vout reduces the gate-source drive.
blocks.answer: The device's own vgs shrinks as the output rises; it is negative feedback.
